rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: World events are understood through regularities of agreement and difference; distinctive breaks in regularity let us distinguish kinds and individuals.
rows.anchor: Fi’l-hakīka vukū‘ât-ı âlem birbirine zıt iki cins ıttırad ile mülâhaza olunmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miracles distinguish prophets from others and confirm their claims; they are a divine custom within the wider regularity of differentiation.
rows.anchor: peygamberlerin “mucize” denilen alâmet-i fârikaları da bu suretle onları diğerlerinden temyiz ettirerek davalarını tasdik etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophecy is an extraordinary event within the human kind, not inferable by reason alone but knowable through observation and report.
rows.anchor: insan nev‘i denilen tevâfuk ıttıradları içinde nübüvvet vâkı‘aları da öyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phenomenon that departs from custom is not thereby impossible; allowing its occurrence entails no contradiction, and reason and science cannot rule it out.
rows.anchor: âdet olmayan böyle bir şeyin imkânına akl ü fennin cevaz vermeyeceğini iddia etmek de akıl ve fen nâmına bir bühtan olurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects using present-day human knowledge to deny transmitted extraordinary events from the past as an unjust, anti-intellectual dogmatism.
rows.anchor: nakledilegelen vâkı‘ât-ı mümtâzeyi inkâr ve tevile sapmaları ilim ve intibâh-ı beşerîye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rigid naturalists overlook that regularities begin with unprecedented changes and that transformations and stages of development also arise through particular extraordinary events.
rows.anchor: bütün tekâmül hududlarının da hep böyle bir hârika-i mahsûsa ile zuhur ettiğini iyi düşünemezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A transformation's speed or scale does not make it contradictory; absolute power has no incapacity, and an abrupt transformation is conceivable.
rows.anchor: aynı hâdisenin birdenbire ve daha büyük bir mikyasta vukū‘unu tasavvur etmekte ve böyle bir vâkı‘ayı müşahede veya ihbar eylemekte tabî‘at-ı inkılâb nokta-i nazarından hiçbir tenakuz yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trusting only in miracles while neglecting customary causes, accumulated knowledge, effort, education, and personal initiative departs from the straight path.
rows.anchor: insanın bütün ümit ve nazarını hârikalara bağlayıp da hilkatteki cereyân-ı âdeti ihmal etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an directs attention especially to law, divine custom, religious law, and method, and condemns innovation.
rows.anchor: Kur’an nazarları hârikalardan ziyade kanun ve sünnete, şer‘e ve minhâca tevcih etmekte ve sünnet-i seniyye, bid‘atçılığı zemmeylemektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying that God can create outside customary patterns limits the Creator's absolute power by a rigid naturalist logic and leads to despair.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın cereyân-ı mu‘tâd hilâfında bir şey yaratamayacağını zannetmek de Hâlık teâlâ’nın kudret-i mutlakasını câmid bir tabiat mantıkıyla tahdîde kalkışmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He warns against limiting the Creator’s absolute power by rigid naturalist logic and recalls that God created the heavens and earth and rules creation and command.
rows.anchor: câmid bir tabiat mantıkıyla tahdîde kalkışmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural laws are generalizations of observed, experimentally tested, and inductively established regularities; causality is the most important such regularity.
rows.anchor: Ittıradların en mühimi de illiyet ıttırâdıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural science has not made all its knowledge into causal laws; even physics and chemistry do not encompass every phenomenon, and biology is further from that state.
rows.anchor: İlm-i hayat ise henüz bu hâlden uzaktır. Fizik ve kimyada da birçok vâkı‘aların, müte‘addid illetlerden her birine ma‘lûl olabildiği müsellemdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One effect can have different causes, and each observed cause belongs to a longer chain of causes and powers that must be considered.
rows.anchor: Meselâ bir fabrikaya, bir su illet-i muharrike olabildiği gibi, bir buhar, bir elektrik de olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human causal knowledge is partial and relative, while ultimate creation requires a total cause and a universal Creator.
rows.anchor: Hakīkī ve mutlak illiyet esasından bir halk u îcâd, illet-i kül de hâlık-ı kül olmak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We may not deny ordinary causes, but cannot treat finite causal knowledge as ultimate or use it to declare an event impossible and attribute incapacity to absolute power.
rows.anchor: illiyet ıttıradları hakkındaki ilmimiz tam ve mutlak değil, cüz’î ve nisbîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a genuine contradiction, where positing something entails its nonexistence, would make an event impossible.
rows.anchor: Meğer ki o şeyin vücûdunu farz etmek onun ‘ademini iktizâ edecek bir tenakuz olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even light turning off at its appearance illustrates how rapidly creation and annihilation can occur.
rows.anchor: sönüşündeki sür‘at bile bize ne kadar serî‘bir surette halk u ifnâlar mümkin olduğunu gösterir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies another class of deniers as people unwilling to accept truth that conflicts with their desires or interests, calling this condition Pharaoh-like tyranny.
rows.anchor: hakk u hakikati kabul etmek istemezler ve onunla mücadele etmek için her haksızlığı irtikâbdan çekinmezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the magicians' public defeat and conversion, Pharaoh claimed the event was a plot and threatened to cut their opposite limbs and crucify them all.
rows.anchor: ellerinizi ve ayaklarınızı çaprazına kestireceğim, sonra da hepinizi elbette ve elbette çarmıha gerdireceğim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had the magicians' faith been a deceitful collusion, Pharaoh's threat would have stopped them; sincere believers instead grow firmer in their resolve against injustice.
rows.anchor: kalbleri mahabbetullah ile çarpan ve âhirete cidden iman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the magicians were known for skill in magic, suspicion about their sincerity was not wholly groundless; public testing removed that doubt.
rows.anchor: Sâhirler mukaddemâ sihirde maharetle mâruf kimseler olduklarından dolayı imanlarında böyle bir mekr ü hile şüphesi büsbütün sebepsiz addolunamazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine wisdom required the magicians to prove publicly and decisively that their faith was sincere and that Moses' miracle was not magic.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ kendilerini hakk u halk muvâcehesinde böyle bir imtihâna tâbi‘tuttu ve muvaffak kıldı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians' response that they would return to their Lord can mean that death is inevitable whether Pharaoh kills them or not, so his threat is powerless.
rows.anchor: Biz nasıl olsa öleceğiz, sen istesen de öleceğiz istemesen de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their response can also mean that execution would make them martyrs who reach their Lord's mercy and reward, so they welcome dying for truth.
rows.anchor: Sen bizi keser, asarsan biz şehid olur ve muhakkak Rabbimizin rahmet ü sevâbına kavuşuruz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possible meaning is that Pharaoh and the magicians will all die and stand before their Lord, who will judge between oppressor and oppressed.
rows.anchor: gerek biz ve gerek sen hepimiz ölüp Rabbimizin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians say Pharaoh resents only their belief in the Lord's signs; accepting evident truth is a virtue, not a crime deserving punishment.
rows.anchor: Hâlbuki sen bizden hiçbir sebeple değil, ancak Rabbimizin âyetlerine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say their recognition of truth is fixed in conscience and cannot be abandoned to please Pharaoh, whose anger exposes injustice and ignorance.
rows.anchor: vicdanlarımızda def‘i nâkābil bir zarûret ile sâbit olan böyle bir idrak ve imandan seni memnun etmek için vazgeçmek de tâkatimizden hâriç bulunduğu hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer asks for patience that will flood and cleanse them, keeping them pure from disbelief, idolatry, deceit, and sin.
rows.anchor: yâ Rabbenâ bize sabır ifâza et yani su gibi her tarafımızı kaplayacak; şirk ü küfr, mekr ü isyan küfürlerinden yıkayacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking to die as Muslims demonstrates the depth and certainty of their faith and their disregard for death.
rows.anchor: imanlarındaki ciddiyeti, îkānlarındaki şiddet ü kuvveti ölümü istihfaf

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that they were magicians in the morning and martyrs by evening; others argued the threat was not carried out because the Qur'an does not state it explicitly, while the author favors its fulfillment from the Qur'anic context.
rows.anchor: Bazıları İbn Abbas’tan “günün evvelinde sâhir idiler, âhirinde şehit oldular” diye nakletmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that Pharaoh executed them: they knowingly remained steadfast and welcomed martyrdom, which also established the sincerity of their faith and the miracle's truth.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bizce siyâk-ı Kur’an vukū‘unu andırıyor. Bu zevât, imanlarında sebat ederek ölmeyi canlarına minnet bilmişler ve hak yolunda şehid olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their martyrdom did not frustrate Moses' miracle, whose purpose was to prove his truth; their actual self-sacrifice made the sincerity of their testimony unmistakable.
rows.anchor: Mucizenin gayesi de Mûsâ’nın davasındaki sıdkını isbat idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's propaganda and terror still affected his people, showing that deceit can have a temporary effect even against truth.
rows.anchor: Firavun’un mekr propagandası ve zulm ü tedhiş siyaseti de kavmi üzerinde icrâ-yı te’sîrden hâlî kalmadığını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking protection means asking the Prophet for safe conduct and shelter from attack after the announced period has ended.
rows.anchor: mühlet-i mezkûre çıktıktan sonra sana istîmân eder, senin kendisine eman verip câr olmanı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protection lets the seeker hear the Qur'an and proofs of truth, reflect, and learn the truth of the invited religion; for a speaker of Arabic, hearing may suffice for understanding.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ı ve delâil-i Hakk’ı işitsin, düşünsün, senin davet ettiğin dinin hakikat ve hakkiyetine muttali‘olmak imkânını elde etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says a polytheist asked Ali whether anyone seeking Muhammad after the deadline to hear God's word or for another need would be killed; Ali answered no and cited this verse.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunur ki Hazret-i Ali’ye müşriklerden bir adam geldi, “bu mühletin inkizâsından sonra şayet bizden bir kimse kelâmullâhı dinlemek için veya diğer bir hâcet için Muhammed’e gelecek olursa katlolunacak mı?” dedi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpreters resolve the apparent conflict with Ali's report by restricting the other need to religious matters, since asking questions and hearing proofs also counts as hearing God's word.
rows.anchor: Bunun için denilmiştir ki hâcetten murad herhangi bir hâcet-i dünyeviye değil, dine müte‘allik hâcettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees no conflict and does not restrict the request to religious needs: the protection request is unrestricted, while listening to God's word describes the grantor's purpose.
rows.anchor: Fakat dikkat olunursa muhalefet yoktur, hâceti böyle tahsise lüzum da yoktur. Zira âyette isticâre mutlaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safe conduct is obligatory when the seeker requests it for a religious purpose, but not obligatory for an unrestricted or worldly purpose; circumstances may make granting or refusing it appropriate or obligatory.
rows.anchor: istîmân ederse eman vermek vâcib olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If an unbeliever seeks proofs of divine unity and prophethood to believe on evidence, Muslims must present the proofs; a belligerent may not be killed before that case is made.
rows.anchor: Bir kâfir, an delîlin itikad etmek için bizden tevhid ve risaletin delâilini beyan ve ikāme-i hüccet talebinde bulunursa tevhîd-i ilâhîyi ve Hazret-i Peygamber’in sıhhat-i nübüvvetini beyan ile ikāme-i hüccet üzerimize vâcib olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The duty to teach also follows when anyone asks for an explanation of a matter relevant to their affairs.
rows.anchor: her kim bizden umûruna müte‘allik bir şeyin târifini talep ve iltimas ederse tâlimi üzerimize vâcib olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists hold that a belligerent entering Islamic territory under protection for a lawful religious purpose or trade is protected, even when the guarantee came from a minor or an insane person.
rows.anchor: Fukaha demişlerdir ki: Bir harbî dâr-ı İslâm’a dâhil oluverirse kendisi ve malı ganimet olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists treat a diplomatic mission as safe conduct, and protection for a person's property as also protecting them when they enter to retrieve it.
rows.anchor: Herhangi birisi dâr-ı İslâm’a bir elçilikle giderse elçilik emandır. Birisi dâr-ı İslâm’daki bir malını almak için gider ve o malın da emânı bulunursa malın emânı onun da emânı olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the visitor has heard the message, escort an unbelieving non-convert safely back to their secure place; a protected visitor may not be detained longer than needed.
rows.anchor: istimâ‘ettikten sonra iman etmezse canı ve malı taarruzdan masûn olarak onu eman yeri olan mahalline, vatanına yetiştir. Binâen‘aleyh müste’menin fazla bir müddet durdurulması da câiz değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called people who do not know because they lack knowledge of faith and its rulings; protection allows them to hear the truth and removes their excuse.
rows.anchor: İman ve İslâm’ın hakikat ve ahkâmını bilmezler ve hatta bu Arab müşrikleri her hususta câhil bir kavimdirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God supplies provisions from heaven and earth and owns, creates, equips, governs, and controls hearing and sight, the most noble faculties and means of using provision.
rows.anchor: Yani o rızıklarla intifâ‘ın en mühim vesâit ve şerâitinden olan his kuvvelerinin en şereflisi bulunan işitme ve görme melekeleri gibi nimeti kim veriyor?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular 'hearing' and plural 'sights' suggest that seeing is more various or numerous than hearing.
rows.anchor: müfred, “ebsâr”ın cemi‘olarak îrâdı görmenin işitmeden kesretli olduğuna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ownership of hearing and sight points to the divine source of recognizing truth, the beginning of certainty, and insight into external reality.
rows.anchor: Fâtiha’da bahsedilen tasdîk-i hak ve

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True hearing, seeing, and perceiving truth are directly divine acts; he also connects this to the sacred hadith on God becoming the servant's hearing through supererogatory devotion.
rows.anchor: doğru görmek ve doğru işitmek, hak ve hakikati hiss ü idrak etmek işinin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life comes from lifeless matter and returns to death: living plants, animals, and people appear, and organic life develops from food and inorganic material.
rows.anchor: Dün ortada yokken bugün bir zîhayat, bir nebat, bir hayvan, bir insan meydana geliyor ve birtakım hayatsız maddelerden çıkıp geliyor. Ve sonra ölüyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These transformations between opposed natures violate sameness and regularity, so they indicate an active power beyond nature that makes causes and effects change places.
rows.anchor: tabiatın kānûn-ı esâsîsi olan ıttırad ve ayniyete muhalif ve binâen‘aleyh hilâf-ı tabiat hâdisâttır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God manages the whole universe's affairs and order by command, not only the acts of creating the particular phenomena named.
rows.anchor: Yani yalnız o zikrolunan husûsât değil, daha bunlar gibi nice ezdâd ve tabâyi‘-i muhtelife ile meşhun olan ale’lumûm âlemin şuûn ve umûrunu tedbir ve idare eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even polytheists readily answer that God does these things when they reflect; the closing question challenges them to fear His power and avoid associating partners and disobeying Him.
rows.anchor: Bu suâllerin cevâbı gayet vâzıh olduğundan müşrikler bile bunları teemmül edince hep bunları Allah yapıyor demekte tereddüt göstermeyeceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one with these perfect attributes, powers, acts, creation, and command is Allah, the true Lord and sole rightful deity, master and authority over people.
rows.anchor: Allah, hak Rabbiniz ulûhiyet münhasıran kendinin hakkı olan tek mâbud, hakikaten ve bi-hakkın mâlikiniz ve veliyyü’l-emriniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no middle position between truth and error: whoever crosses beyond truth falls into error, and every creed other than monotheism is misguidance.
rows.anchor: hak ile dalâl beyninde vâsıta yoktur. Hakkı tecavüz eden mutlak dalâlete düşmüş bulunur. Hak teâlâ’dan gayrı rab ma‘dûm ve bâtıl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse challenges how people are turned from truth to error, monotheism to association, and happiness to calamity, asking where they are being led.
rows.anchor: Yani haktan dalâle, tevhidden şirke, saadetten nekbete nasıl çevriliyorsunuz? Dalâle sarf olunmaya nasıl râzı oluyorsunuz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being upon clear proof from one's Lord means having reason and understanding; God's witness that follows is the Qur'an's miracle, which confirms the proof.
rows.anchor: Rabbinden bir beyyine üzerine olan yani akl ü iz‘ânı bulunan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' earlier Book serves as an imam and mercy and a further witness to the person with proof and the Qur'an's testimony.
rows.anchor: daha evvelinden de bir imam ve rahmet olarak Mûsâ’nın kitabı, şâhidi bulunan kimse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people described are Muhammad and his companions, who believe in Islam; anyone among the factions who rejects it has the Fire as destination.
rows.anchor: yani Muhammed ve ashâbı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority do not believe because they lack sound reason and a straight conscience, with worldly desires blinding their hearts.
rows.anchor: Çünkü akl-ı selimleri ve vicdân-ı müstakīmleri yoktur, hayât-ı dünya şehevâtıyla kalbleri körlenmiştir

none: Verse translation only; no independent commentary or other point is made.
Verse translation and a transition only; no independent commentary on the verses is given.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks why earlier generations did not reach the exclusive worship and guidance Moses describes, thus seeking to deny divine guidance and prophethood.
rows.anchor: kurûn-ı ûlâ neye o hidâyete ermemiş, niçin senin dediğin gibi ihlâs ve tevhid ile ibadet etmemiş de putlara tapmış?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Pharaoh means generations before him, he does not separate himself from them; in Qur'anic usage, those earliest generations end with his destruction in al-Qasas.
rows.anchor: Firavun “kurûn-ı ûlâ” demekle kendi zamanına tekaddüm eden karnları kast etmiş olmakla beraber kendisi de onlardan ayrılmak istemediği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses avoids claiming knowledge of the generations' fate and instead says their knowledge is with God, recorded in a Book; God neither errs nor forgets.
rows.anchor: onların hâli bana gāibdir, gayba ilim de ancak Rabbimin indinde bir kitaptadır. Onların hâli ne olduğunu ve ne olacağını ancak O bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave them guidance, but they did not accept it; the earth as cradle and provision of plants are visible signs of that guidance.
rows.anchor: O yol göstermiş, onlar kabul etmemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about producing varied plants, the discourse shifts grammatically from speaking of God in the third person to the first person.
rows.anchor: Burada gıyabdan tekellüme iltifat vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuhā means reason, which restrains a person from following falsehood and evil.
rows.anchor: “Nühâ” bâtıla ve fena şeylere uymaktan nehyeden akıl demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and their benefits are not toys; they are signs of power created with truth and wisdom so people may know God and prepare for eternal life.
rows.anchor: hak ve hikmetle yaratılmış burhân-ı kudrettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If creation served only worldly human life, it would be mere play as 47:36 and 57:20 state; disbelievers who think only of this life try to make the universe their plaything.
rows.anchor: mantûkunca bir lehv ü la‘ibden ibaret olmak lâzım gelirdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressors may want to play, but creation is no toy and its Creator is not playing.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı o zâlimler ne kadar oynamak isterse istesin hilkat oyuncak değil, Hâlık oyuncu hiç değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of taking amusement from God's presence means a purely divine amusement, which would itself be true wisdom rather than frivolity.
rows.anchor: elbette onu ledünnümüzden ittihaz ederdik yani sırf ilâhî bir lehv ittihaz ederdik. Ve o hâlde o bir lehv değil ayn-ı hikmet olurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means making an amusement for God Himself, not for people; either way, God does not do so, since play is incompatible with the perfection of the All-Wise.
rows.anchor: Yahut âlemi onlar tarafından eğlenmek üzere bir eğlence değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument is that if the supposed consequence is false, its antecedent is false too; play cannot be ascribed to God.
rows.anchor: Tâlî bâtıl binâen‘aleyh mukaddem de öyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are called Companions of Eyke, or of Leyke according to the Leyke reading; Eyke is a marshy place with soft trees by the sea toward Midian.
rows.anchor: “Eyke” yumuşak ağaç bitiren bataklık demek olup Medyen’e doğru sâhil-i bahrda bir mevki‘in ismidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shu'ayb was sent to the people living there but was an outsider, which explains why the Qur'an does not call him their brother.
rows.anchor: Şuayb aleyhisselâm bunlara da meb‘us olmuş idi. Lâkin onlardan değil, ecnebi idi. Onun için “ehûhum” denilmeyerek sadece “Şuayb” buyurulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also said that Leyke was the name of the central town, so the Companions of Eyke could mean the Companions of al-Hijr.
rows.anchor: merkezleri olan kasabanın ismi de deniliyor. Yani Leyke ashâb-ı Hıcr’in merkez şehirleri imiş. Şu hâlde “Ashâbü’l-Eyke”, “Ashâbü’l-Hıcr” demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage indicates that these people were engaged in trade and were unjust and deceitful.
rows.anchor: Bunların ticaret ile meşgul oldukları ve zâlim ve hîlekâr bulundukları anlaşılıyor
